title: Sustainable Financing Partnership
summary: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment in Dubai reports that AI credit and eligibility models automate housing-loan assessment, but no source measures their separate effect.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment (MBRHE) in Dubai reports that AI models evaluate housing-loan eligibility and priority using credit, income and social criteria. It identifies logistic regression, decision trees and ensemble models trained with historical approvals and credit-bureau data. MBRHE says that it piloted the service at 20 customer centers in the second quarter of 2024 and issued over 2,100 loans in the first six months. It dates full deployment to the first quarter of 2025. MBRHE describes the models as removing manual approval bottlenecks within a service integrated with Emirates Islamic Bank. Bank financing, interest subsidies, links to bank systems through application programming interfaces (APIs) and digital identity also contribute to the overall program. The program's figures for loan volume, budget savings and workload do not isolate the models’ contribution. On 7 December 2025 MBRHE signed a housing-finance agreement with Dubai Islamic Bank that sets up electronic exchange of documents and transactions. In October 2026 Emirates Islamic states that it still assesses each applicant's eligibility under Central Bank rules after MBRHE approval.
purpose: Reduce manual work and delays in housing-loan eligibility assessment.
system: MBRHE AI housing-loan credit and eligibility assessment
developer: Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment and unnamed private technology vendors
deployer: Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment and Emirates Islamic Bank
